item.title: Nations Meet in Armenia as Goal to Protect Nature Remains Out of Reach
item.description: The United Nations is convening delegates from nearly 200 countries to try to make progress on pledges to protect plants, animals and ecosystems.

item.title: El Niño Threatens Global Sugar Supply
item.description: A sugarcane crop withered by El Niño in India, the world’s second-largest producer, is hurting consumers and farmers — plus undermining the country’s energy security goals.
item.dc:creator: Somini Sengupta, Suhasini Raj and Anindito Mukherjee
item.media:description: A worker tending to a sugarcane crop in Maharashtra, India, in September.

item.title: How One Global Climate Deal Worked ‘Perfectly’ as Others Faltered

item.media:credit: Qilai Shen for The New York Times
item.media:description: A plant in China that was producing HFC, a refrigerant, in 2012. Use of the chemical, a planet-warming greenhouse gas, has fallen sharply.

item.title: Amit Forlit, the Israeli Private Eye at the Heart of a Climate Hacking Scandal

item.title: Bleached Coral Rebounded After Touching Healthy Coral, Study Finds
item.description: After sick corals were placed in direct contact with healthy ones of the same genetic makeup, they recovered at “incredible” speed, scientists found.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Zhong

item.title: See How El Niño Is Washing Ashore in California

item.title: Energy Firms Try to Squeeze More Power Out of Old Nuclear Plants

item.title: Melting Ice Reveals Artifacts in the Swiss Alps
